name: Arcadia-Jezero Smooth Terrace
rationale: Low-elevation smooth volcanic plain (-2540 m MOLA) offering thick atmospheric column for heavy lander aerobraking and <2 deg baseline slope.
primary_resources: Subsurface water-ice sheet, basaltic regolith for radiation shielding, unobstructed solar horizon

name: Jezero Western Delta Apron
rationale: Ancient lacustrine delta front with hydrated phyllosilicate clays and flat alluvial bench in coarse MOLA baseline imagery.
primary_resources: Hydrated clay minerals, sedimentary aggregates, proximity to ancient lakebed deposits

name: Nili Fossae Regolith Bench
rationale: Consolidated basaltic plateau sheltered from regional dust storm corridors with stable load-bearing bedrock.
primary_resources: Olivine/carbonate outcrops, high-strength basalt bedrock, high solar insolation

name: Shackleton Sunlit Rim Alpha
rationale: Elevated South Pole crater rim crest (+1720 m LOLA) with quasi-continuous solar illumination (>85% of lunar year) adjacent to cold-trap volatiles.
primary_resources: Permanently shadowed crater water-ice (<2 km), near-continuous solar power, Earth RF visibility

name: Connecting Ridge Basecamp
rationale: Broad topographic saddle linking Shackleton and de Gerlache rims; combines flat landing terrain with dual cold-trap access.
primary_resources: Anorthositic regolith (oxygen extraction), solar ridge exposure, low-grade rover traverse routes

name: Malapert Massif Southern Bench
rationale: High-altitude highland terrace maintaining uninterrupted direct line-of-sight to Earth for autonomous telemetry and crewed comms.
primary_resources: Uninterrupted Earth communications relay vantage, ilmenite/anorthosite regolith, thermal stability
